lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.summ: Study an oblique sea turtle pose, refine natural contours and overlapping flippers, then add restrained shell texture that follows the form.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.step: Observe the shell as an oblique natural contour, not a perfect oval, then mark its main flow direction.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.help: Compare the two ends of the shell. Let one end feel narrower so the form turns through space.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.comp: The shell contour now carries a clear viewpoint.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.step: Build the neck with two different curves and taper it into a compact head.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.help: Avoid a tube with parallel sides. Let the neck subtly widen where it joins the shell.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.comp: The head and neck now connect as one natural form.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.step: Shape the near front and rear flippers with long tapered contours and clear overlap at the shell.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.help: Watch where each flipper disappears behind or emerges from the shell edge.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.comp: The near flippers give the pose weight and direction.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.step: Add smaller far flippers and keep more of them hidden so depth stays believable.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.help: The far flippers should not compete with the near ones in size or length.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.comp: Good depth. The near and far sides now read differently.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.step: Add a few shell scutes and edge marks that bend with the shell instead of flattening it.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.help: Use fewer marks and make each one follow the form. Texture should explain the surface, not cover it.
lesson.sea_turtle_observation_glide.comp: The restrained texture finishes the observational study.
